subject.title: [Bug]: External Control UI tab cannot render gateway-auth plugin route under token auth

question: Should external plugin tabs receive narrowly delegated HTTP authority through the linked PR's signed HttpOnly launch cookie, or should the host use a different authenticated proxy/session mechanism?
rationale: This choice creates a new browser-to-Gateway credential-delegation boundary, so cookie scope, replay, CSRF behavior, route ownership, and operator-scope semantics require explicit maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve bounded launch session
options.body: Use a short-lived signed HttpOnly session only after proving plugin-root binding, minimal scopes, expiry, replay limits, browser behavior, and continued unauthenticated denial.

options.title: Require host-mediated proxy
options.body: Keep plugin routes free of delegated cookies and route iframe requests through a host-owned authenticated proxy with equivalent path and scope confinement.

options.title: Withdraw authenticated tab contract
options.body: Document external tabs as public or plugin-auth-managed only, which avoids delegation complexity but breaks the currently documented gateway-route integration.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded launch session
recommendation.body: Use a short-lived signed HttpOnly session only after proving plugin-root binding, minimal scopes, expiry, replay limits, browser behavior, and continued unauthenticated denial.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person most directly to both Gateway authorization and plugin registry boundaries affected by the decision.
